question: Should agent-behavior governance become a permanent core `security.behaviorPolicy` contract, or remain an optional plugin built on the existing lifecycle hooks?
rationale: The choice defines a new security/configuration contract and determines whether core gains a second prompt, execution, and delivery-policy pipeline; code review alone cannot establish that product boundary.

options.title: Use a governance plugin
options.body: Keep core lean and implement rules through `before_prompt_build`, `before_tool_call`, `before_agent_finalize`, and `message_sending`, adding only any proven missing SDK seam.

options.title: Sponsor a core contract
options.body: Retain core configuration only after redesigning it around the canonical schema, all prompt harnesses, pre-delivery gating, explicit failure modes, upgrade documentation, and live proof.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Close the proposal if OpenClaw does not want to present heuristic model-output checks as a security-governance product surface.

recommendation.title: Use a governance plugin
recommendation.body: Keep core lean and implement rules through `before_prompt_build`, `before_tool_call`, `before_agent_finalize`, and `message_sending`, adding only any proven missing SDK seam.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a project-level core-versus-plugin and security-contract decision.
